### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54ea3c8c383c0fb83f8af7efb32a677c5bb46db0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6e0b42e7389a0f969697a39e93e37793e2c342a2` — the merge of head `02da5d4e3f7b58b5c0ec1ac0cc7488dd707ed85f` into base `54ea3c8c383c0fb83f8af7efb32a677c5bb46db0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6e0b42e7389a0f969697a39e93e37793e2c342a2 && git checkout 6e0b42e7389a0f969697a39e93e37793e2c342a2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
```

repo:objectstack#6 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjQkY5yXZrN9BEA3rEK

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `02da5d4e3f7b58b5c0ec1ac0cc7488dd707ed85f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/ChatbotEnhanced.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useAiModels.ts

Inputs read: card #35578 (body and all 5 comments, every one from `objectstack-fleet[bot]`), PR #37519 (body, 9 files, net diff against `main` from merge-base `df0894a6`; `main` is now `54ea3c8c` and none of the 9 paths moved there), and the check-runs on the head: 61 success, 9 expected skips, none red, none pending. Read to judge, not reviewed: `protocol.zod.ts` and `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` on `main`; `AGENTS.md`; `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/cross-repo-coordination.md`; in the cloud checkout at `58bdf6a`, `packages/service-ai/src/routes/ai-routes.ts`, `packages/service-tenant/src/objects/sys-ai-model.object.ts` and cloud ADR-0028.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public type of `@objectstack/spec`.** The object arm of `AiModelsResponseSchema.models[]` gains `tierLabel?: string`, so the exported `AiModelsResponse` (the return type of `client.ai.models()` in `@objectstack/client`) widens by one optional key. Additive, and declared as such. Right.
2. **Parse accept set.** The arm is a non-strict `z.object`, so before this change an entry carrying `tierLabel` with any value parsed and the key was stripped. Now `''`, a non-string and `null` under that key are refused. By the letter that narrows the set for a key that was undeclared. Judged not a narrowing in the sense the `Clause-②:` line asks about, on three readings: no producer writes the key (cloud `pickerModelsWithCostMultiplier` emits `id`, `label`, `default`, `costMultiplier` only; the fallback arm returns the adapter's `listModels()` list, which this diff does not touch); nothing in this tree parses a live response with the schema (its only readers are `protocol.test.ts`, the type export and the type-alias pin); and #33746 set the classification for the identical shape on the same entry (`costMultiplier: z.number().positive().optional()`, declared `yes (widening)`, "Nothing is removed or narrowed"). Right, with the letter recorded here.
3. **`z.input` equals `z.infer`.** The key has no default and no transform, so the `Iso_api_protocol__AiModelsResponseSchema` pin still holds; `TypeScript Type Check` is green on the head. Right.
4. **Public surface of `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`.** `ChatbotModelOption` gains `tierLabel?: string` and `useAiModels().models` can carry it. No export is added, removed or renamed. Additive. Right.
5. **Generated reference.** `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` carries the new row with the `.describe()` text word for word, and the `models` type cell gains `tierLabel?: string`. The job that holds every spec artifact gate is green on the head. Right.
6. **Behaviour for every response served today.** The closed trigger's text changes only for an entry that carries `tierLabel`; the trigger's `title`, the list rows, the `×20` question and the id a pick writes are untouched. No served response carries the key, so nothing a user sees moves at merge. Right, and the changeset says so.
7. **Liveness.** The ledgers under `packages/spec/liveness/` cover metadata types and hold no row for this response schema; none is owed. The key lands with a reader in the same diff, so it is not a carrier with zero consumers. `Spec property liveness` is green on the head.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and on `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`, with `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and on the changeset. All three are right.

- `Metadata-protocol: none`: the key sits on a service response, not on anything a metadata author writes. AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3: the level follows the kind alone, and `none` takes `patch`, "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`".
- `Clause-②: yes`: the public type of both packages widens (① 1 and 4). The arm is optional under the same step, and `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- Precedent: #33746 shipped the sibling key under 18.5.0 Patch Changes with the same pair of lines.
- Both packages the diff moves are named in the one changeset; no other published package is touched.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]`, display string or tier id: answered in ④ (a). Keep `tierLabel`.
- `out_of_scope_findings[0]`, the key lands before its producer: answered in ④ (b). It may land.
- `out_of_scope_findings[1]`, four gate families the dev's box could not measure: the head's check-runs are the gate answer, and every one of them is success or an expected skip.
- PR acceptance note, the trigger's `title` no longer equals its text: judged in ④, it holds.
- The docs sentence outside the claim's declared file surface (`content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`) is a prose face: the lane seat's read, not this record's.
- Route comment 7077739326 ("the picker half lands with the cloud half, never alone") is a fleet seat's statement, not a maintainer ruling, and the later triage comment 7118572418 and the card body both say the cloud card follows once the key lands. Weighed in ④ (b).
- SQL push-down: the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no join. Nothing to flag.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no off-relay note is owed.
- AGENTS.md Prime Directive 13 asks for an ADR grep on the surface touched: `docs/adr/**` and `ui/docs/adr/**` hold no decision on the model list or the picker. The governing record is cloud ADR-0028, which the schema docblock already cites; see the cloud item at the end of ④.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`** (the one `hits` file), judged against what it implements, item 5 of #35445 (the closed picker shows the tier name only, 「快速」) through card #35578 step 1, and against its first consumer, `ModelPicker` in this diff. The change holds.

**(a) Key shape: a display string `tierLabel`, or a tier id.** The display string is the right shape. On precedent and on each of the four axes:

- *Spec precedent.* The entry already pairs a machine `id` with a server-supplied display `label`; `tierLabel` is a second display string beside it, named the way the spec names such siblings (`pluralLabel` beside `label` in `data/object.zod.ts`, `confirmLabel` in `ui/bulk-action.zod.ts`, `addLabel` in `ui/view.zod.ts`). The same file already states that a response carries labels the server localised ("labels in the request locale", the Studio form of a metadata type). No response schema in `api/` carries a tier id, and the spec has no model-tier vocabulary anywhere.
- *Real business need.* Measured, not assumed: #35445 read the hosted console in zh-CN showing the closed picker cut to 「Fast · Claude Haiku…」 at 179px, and the maintainer's card asks for the tier name alone. What that needs is one short string a person reads. Nobody reads or writes a tier id: cloud has none. In cloud the tier word is free text an operator types inside `sys_ai_model.label` (cloud ADR-0028 D5 and D8, "tier · name"), so an id would have to be invented on both sides to serve a need that is only a display name.
- *Long-term soundness.* An id needs a closed set in the open spec, or an open string the console maps. A closed set puts cloud's commercial naming into the open contract and makes every new tier a spec release plus a cloud pin move. An open string leaves the console to decide what to draw for an id it has no text for. The display string keeps one owner for the words, the service that also owns `label`.
- *Preventing AI mistakes, declared must be enforced.* With an id the console needs a mapping and a default for the unmapped case: either a raw machine value on screen (the North Star AI row sets the bar that internal values are never shown) or a silent drop back to `label`, the kind of consumer-side fallback the third axis warns will hide a mistake. With the string there is nothing to map. The schema states the domain (`.min(1)`), the wire reader keeps the key only inside that domain, and a blank closed picker cannot be produced through the hook.
- *Startup no-sprawl.* The string costs one optional key and one read. The id costs an enum, console translations in every locale, and a second vocabulary to keep in step across two repositories.

One correction to the PR body's reasoning, which does not change the outcome: the model tier is not cloud's plan tier. Plan tiers (`free`, `team`, `business`, `enterprise`) live on `available_for_plans`; the model tier word is operator text in the label. That makes the case for a string stronger, since there is no vocabulary to make an id from.

A neutral name such as a short label was considered and set aside: the card and the maintainer's item both name the tier, and the docblock says what the string is, not only where it is drawn.

**(b) May the optional key land before its producer.** Yes. The existing rules settle the order; this is not a fork for the maintainer.

- *The dependency direction is fixed.* `cross-repo-coordination.md`: 「依赖方向固定:objectstack(后端与 ui/,packages/spec 唯一契约)→ cloud、hotcrm、mobile」. AGENTS.md Prime Directive 12 makes `packages/spec` "the one contract between metadata producers and the runtime/renderers that consume it". A producer in cloud that wrote the key first would be writing a key its pinned spec does not declare. Across two repositories and a pin, spec first is the only contract-first order.
- *What must not land alone is a key without a reader, and this one has its reader.* Same file, rule 2: 「main 有 ui/ 起,新 spec 键不再先行…与首个读者同 PR」 and 「⛔ planned 行不单独进 main」, where `planned` is a carrier with zero consumers (`dispatch-runbook.md`). The first reader, the picker, is in this PR.
- *The producer half has a prescribed carrier.* Same file, rule 3: 「已验收 PR 的产物流向另一仓,接受该 PR 的执行席立即在消费仓立后续单,带 Blocked-by:」, with the pin probe `git merge-base --is-ancestor` beside it. The seat's plan, a cloud card at ACCEPT, is that rule.
- *Declared is not the same as enforced* (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 10: "never advertise or demo a capability the runtime doesn't actually deliver"). The capability declared is: a served `tierLabel` is what the closed picker shows. The runtime in this diff delivers exactly that, pinned in both directions by tests in this diff (tiered, and untiered as before); the PR body reports three ablations of those pins, which were not re-run here. Nothing in the schema, the changeset or the docs sentence says a service serves it today; the changeset says "until it does, the picker looks as it does today". ADR-0049 governs security properties, but its test for enforced is the useful one here: "a runtime consumer reads it and changes a decision". One does.
- *Precedent.* #33746 landed `costMultiplier` on this entry in this order, key and console reader first with the sentence "until it does, the picker looks as it did"; cloud's producer followed, and #35445 read the multipliers live four days later.
- The route comment's "never alone" is met in substance by rule 3 when the cloud card is filed in the same stroke as ACCEPT. As a colleague's statement it ranks below the rule text either way.

What the rules do not settle, and what this record does not rule: **where cloud takes the tier name from.** cloud ADR-0028 D5 says 「`sys_ai_model.label` 是唯一 UI 展示来源」, and that label is one operator-written string in one language. Serving a second display string, in the request's language, amends D5. Under AGENTS.md Prime Directive 13 that decision lives in the cloud registry and is the maintainer's. It belongs on the cloud card as a decision item. It does not gate this PR, because the open contract only says what a served tier name is and what the console does with it.

**`ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/useAiModels.ts`** (implementing). `tierLabelOf` keeps the key only as a string of length 1 or more, which is the schema's `.min(1)` and nothing wider; `normalize` omits the key otherwise, so "absent" is the only other state the picker sees. It mirrors `costMultiplierOf` line for line. Agrees with the contract.

**`ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/ChatbotEnhanced.tsx`** (implementing). Read against the schema's `.describe()` sentence by sentence: "The closed picker shows it in place of `label`" is `shown = models[at].tierLabel ?? inForce` on the trigger; "the open list keeps `label`" is the unchanged row (`m.label ?? m.id`); "absent, the picker shows `label`" is the `??` arm, which is the spec-legal absent case and not tolerance of an off-spec value. The `title` stays the full label, so the model's name is one hover away, and the `×20` question still names the model in full. A selected id outside the list shows the id, as before. Tried to break it with an entry without `label`, an id outside the list and a pick at or above the threshold: each draws what the docblocks say. The bare-string arm cannot carry the key and is untouched by this diff. Agrees with the contract.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — the `.describe()` ends "the picker shows `label` as before". "As before" is release-note wording inside a published docblock and its generated reference row; "absent, the closed picker shows `label`" says the same without a history. Left as an accepted deviation: a fix would move a reviewed schema file.
- N2 (nit) — "in the language the response is served in" names what the same file elsewhere calls "the request locale". Same meaning. Accepted deviation, or folded into the next change that touches the entry.
- N3 (nit) — unlike its sibling, the docblock does not name the writer (`costMultiplier` says "Written by cloud service-ai's GET /api/v1/ai/models"). True as written; the writer's name can arrive with the cloud half.
- N4 (nit) — `ModelPicker` trusts `tierLabel` as typed, where `drawnMultiplierOf` re-reads `costMultiplier` at the picker. A host that passes `models` itself with an empty string would get a blank trigger. The only in-tree source is `useAiModels`, which cannot produce that, and a whitespace-only name passes the schema and the reader alike, so the two agree. Accepted deviation.

For the cloud card the seat files at ACCEPT (hand-off, not findings on this diff): `Blocked-by:` this PR and the pin probe (rule 3); the tier name served in the request's language, since 「快速」 is the card's own example and the label is English in a zh-CN session today; the D5 decision item above; a note that two models sharing one tier name read the same on the closed picker, so names should be distinct within one served list or the ambiguity accepted on purpose; and the sentence that if the cloud half is declined, `tierLabel` is retired here and not left without a producer (the no-sprawl axis: a published capability nobody uses gets no sunk-cost exemption).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-35578-model-tier-key`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Q4EjjQkY5yXZrN9BEA3rEK`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

**L1: ACCEPT** at head `02da5d4e3f7b58b5c0ec1ac0cc7488dd707ed85f` (open, draft, base `main`, mergeable_state clean). Read against GitHub and the tree, not against the report.

**Shape and card relation** (`l1-face.mjs --pr 37519`: 13 items read, none flagged)

- First line `Fixes #35578`. No closing keyword binds another card, and the body read by eye names no other issue number.
- `Fixes` is right. The card's Done-when ("With a tier-bearing entry, the closed picker reads the tier name only. Without one, it reads today's label. Both cases are pinned.") is met by this diff, and the card body puts step 2 on a separate card ("A cloud-side card follows once the key lands"). Condition, in the landing to-do below: the cloud card exists before this merges, so closing #35578 never leaves step 2 untracked.

**Scope and changeset**

- No `content/docs/releases/` path. One changeset, `patch`, names both published packages the diff touches (`@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`), with `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and on the changeset. Kind `none`, so no `Skills-docs:` line is owed.
- One file outside the claim's declared surface: `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`, +3/-1. Accepted as a deviation. `ui/AGENTS.md` rule #2 (docs-driven) requires the matching `content/docs/frontend/` page, the report and the PR body both name the addition, and it is the feature's own page, not a neighbouring fix. The package README does not describe the model picker, so nothing is owed there.
- Sentences read against the diff:
  - Changeset, "the model entry gains an optional `tierLabel`, a non-empty string": true (`z.string().min(1).optional()`).
  - Changeset, "Nothing is removed or narrowed … an entry without `tierLabel` parses as before": true for every entry a producer writes today. By the letter, an entry carrying an off-domain `tierLabel` was stripped before and is refused now; #33746 declared the same shape as widening, and the contract review on this head weighs it.
  - Changeset, "The full `label` stays the picker's tooltip and the text of its row in the open list": true (`title={inForce}`; row text `m.label ?? m.id`).
  - Changeset, "`useAiModels` keeps a served `tierLabel` only when it is a non-empty string": true (`tierLabelOf`).
  - Changeset, "until it does, the picker looks as it does today": true. Cloud `pickerModelsWithCostMultiplier` at cloud `58bdf6a` writes `id`, `label`, `default` and `costMultiplier` only.
  - `plugin-chatbot.mdx`, "Closed, the picker shows the model's `tierLabel` (its tier name alone) when the entry carries one, and its `label` otherwise; the open list always shows the `label`": true against `ModelPicker` (`shown`, and the row text).
  - `references/api/protocol.mdx`: generated; the new row is the `.describe()` text word for word.
- Published docblocks this diff writes (`protocol.zod.ts` `.describe()`, `ChatbotModelOption.tierLabel`, `tierLabelOf`, the `ModelPicker` note): each sentence is true of the code at this head.
- No one-shot codegen in the diff, no move or split, no deletion.

**Tests and gates**

- Check-runs at this head: 61 success, 9 expected skips, 0 red, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Check Changeset`, `Test Core`, `Test UI` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` all read success.
- The report's code readings are at `8a2ba56c`. `8a2ba56c..02da5d4e` is the one docs file (`git diff --stat`: 1 file, +3/-1), and CI ran on `02da5d4e`. Entered.
- The evidence carries real commands with counts: spec 898 files and 28488 tests; plugin-chatbot 103 files and 1079 tests, after a dependency-closure build. Three ablations are reported as positive controls, each turning the new pin red. They were not re-run here.
- The refusal cases (`''`, `3`, `null`) assert `success` is `false`, and the reported ablation that drops `.min(1)` turns them red, so the green is a refusal's green. They are schema parses, not HTTP refusals, so no `code` or `status` assertion is owed.
- `dogfood_battery`: not owed (no `!` in the title, no `(narrowing)` arm).
- No API read in the report that git could have answered.

**Benefit past the boundary**

- The value depends on a producer in another repository. The wire leg is pinned (`useAiModels` reading a served body) and the draw leg is pinned (`ModelPicker`). The key rides the same entry as `costMultiplier`, which #35445 read live on a hosted environment. The live path with a real producer is NOT MEASURED, because no producer exists yet; it becomes an acceptance line on the cloud card.

**Premise**

- Re-read on `origin/main` at `54ea3c8c`: the model entry has no tier field and the closed trigger draws `label ?? id`. Holds.

**Deviations and notes**

- The docs page above: accepted.
- The PR body says the tier vocabulary is cloud's plan tiers. It is not. Plan tiers sit on `available_for_plans`; the model tier is a word the operator types inside `sys_ai_model.label` (cloud ADR-0028 D5 and D8). The conclusion the sentence supports is unchanged. Corrected in the body (no head move); not carried into the cloud card.
- The last Human Minimum box is unticked with its reason, the repo-wide `pnpm lint` left to CI. `Lint & Repo Gates` is green on this head.
- Dev `out_of_scope_findings[0]`, the key lands before its producer: carried by objectstack-ai/cloud#5022, filed at ACCEPT.
- Dev `out_of_scope_findings[1]`, readings the shared box could not take: dropped — environment state, and CI measured this head.
- Dev `open_questions[0]`, display string or tier id: answered by the contract review on this head (keep `tierLabel`).
- Pre-existing and untouched, noted only: `normalize` in `useAiModels` drops bare-string entries, the other arm the schema declares. Not judged in this round.

**Landing to-do, recorded at ACCEPT**

1. Done: objectstack-ai/cloud#5022 filed in the same stroke (cross-repo rule 3) with `Blocked-by:` this PR and the pin probe. It carries: the tier name served in the request's language; the cloud ADR-0028 D5 decision item (the label is today the only display source); distinct tier names within one served list; and the retirement of `tierLabel` here if the cloud half is declined.
2. Done: contract review record 7190559193 (PASS) is on the PR for this head before it leaves draft, and every check is green at that moment.
